scope: All 32 source/student pairs reviewed on the contact sheet; requested IDs 000, 004, 025, 028, 030 additionally viewed at native 1024px each. No extra model inference beyond the completed 32-sample evaluation.
summary: Faces are broadly preserved and remain diverse relative to their own sources; recognizable priest clothing does not generalize to any of the five native-reviewed adult male examples. Local darkening/texture changes are not sufficient to call the model a priest generator.

records.face: Recognizable source face, coherent eyes/nose/mouth and fixed framing. Some contrast and lower-face/neck texture change; no gross double features.
records.clothing: White open shirt remains white. Lower-neck boundary darkens and gains texture; no white clerical tab in black clerical clothing.

records.face: Smile, hair, eyes and face silhouette remain recognizable and coherent. No gross facial collapse.
records.clothing: Original pale garment remains; new irregular dark stippling/blotches near the lower-left neckline look like a stain rather than a clerical conversion.

records.face: Mature male source identity, three-quarter pose, eyes, hair and expression appear retained, with changed local contrast and neck texture.
records.clothing: Striped conventional shirt remains; its folds/stripes are darkened. No priest tab appears.
issues: Darkened clothing retains original non-clerical structure.

records.face: Held-out bearded identity, smile, eyes and beard detail remain broadly intact. No collapse to the training identity.
records.clothing: Original jacket and conventional white shirt edges remain beneath beard; changes around lower neck are small and do not create a central clerical tab.
issues: Little central neck space remains below beard.
The separately created imagegen edit for028 was not used by this one-pair training run.

records.face: Recognizable short-haired source face, eyes, expression and framing remain, with small local shading/texture changes.
records.clothing: Thin original neckline gains dark strokes/textured edging; a recognizable white priest tab is absent.
issues: Preexisting partial second person at left edge retained, not newly introduced.

contact_sheet_findings: Many source women remain women, children remain children (including 008, 019, 026), and headwear remains on 021, 023, 027. The adult bareheaded male sampling requirement is unsolved.
No obvious wholesale identity collapse on the contact sheet. This small fixed set is not a statistical diversity or identity guarantee.
New darkening mainly affects lower regions but can create unwanted neckline texture, most apparent on004.
No production quality or selection yield is inferred from low grayscale MAE.
metrics_caveat: Unclipped luminance MAE on fixed top75/bottom25 regions; these are not detected face/clothing masks, identity scores, collar recognition, or perceptual quality measures. Background and hair contribute. Values can exceed1 if raw generator luminance is out of range.
recommendation: Do not deploy or extend this single-pair run automatically as though collars were solved. The stable faces make a separately bounded multi-pair clothing-supervision experiment reasonable, with reviewed masks and held-out identities; inspect neck artifacts and collar recognition explicitly. Adult male/barehead sampling needs a separate validated solution.
